title: Platform Advocate Evidence & Ask Playbook
author: Priya Menon
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook equips platform advocates (platform engineers, infra leads, and SRE champions inside prospect orgs) with a compact evidence kit and a repeatable set of asks to accelerate pilot approvals and secure committed Dedicated/Private conversations. It bundles messaging, adversarial questions and counters, a short competitive snapshot, pilot pricing scenarios, and a lightweight security FAQ that maps to typical RFP checkpoints.

Intended audience:
- Platform engineers / infrastructure owners
- SRE and reliability leads
- Security architects evaluating deployment models
- Product managers owning LLM feature roadmap

Topline positioning (one-liner for advocates):
- "Ship LLM features with predictable latency, real unit economics, and enterprise-grade controls — from sandbox to private deployment without rebuilding your serving stack."

Key attributes to emphasize to platform stakeholders:
- Predictability: SLA-backed Dedicated offering and deterministic latency for 95th/99th percentiles. Example: 95th-token-latency target = 150ms for 4k context models on p4-equivalent nodes.
- Portability: same API and rollout semantics across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Cost controls: Token-level cost visibility, auto-batching knobs, and quantization advisory for 30–60% TCO reductions on typical chat workloads.
- Reliability & resilience: Cross-region fallbacks, model-variant routing, and transparent degradation paths.

Stakeholder-specific talking points (short bullets you can use verbatim)
- Platform Engineer: "Redwood gives you a single endpoint and a config surface for batching, caching and autoscaling — no model infra to maintain. You keep ownership of the network and KMS."
- SRE Lead: "We provide SLO dashboards, token-level latency histograms, and an error budget alerting pattern you can hook into PagerDuty. Rollouts support canary and A/B with instant rollback."
- Security Architect: "Private deployment options provide a customer-managed control plane with HSM/KMS integrations and audit logs forwarded to your SIEM via syslog or S3."
- Product Manager: "We ship predictable request economics and offer prompt regressions detection tied to evaluators so feature regressions are caught before release."

Competitive snapshot (how to frame Redwood vs three archetypes)
- Cloud AI endpoints: "Easier to start, but limited routing and cost control. Redwood wins when predictable cost and cross-environment parity matter."
- LLM endpoint-only vendors: "Fast API but opaque performance profiles; Redwood provides verified performance profiles and deterministic latency tuning."
- Self-hosted runtimes + orchestration: "Max control but high ops burden. Redwood offers near-self-host control with much lower operational overhead and out-of-the-box fallbacks."

Quick win proof points (short evidence pieces to present in a pilot brief)
- Latency profile: 95th token latency = 150ms, 99th token latency = 260ms (internal benchmark on batch=8, 4k context, gpt-style model).
- Cost delta example: Chat application (1M tokens / month) — typical unit cost saving 38% using recommended batching + int8 quantization path vs baseline hosted single-request mode.
- Reliability story: Canary rollback demonstration completed for customer X (internal case id: CX-2025-114); rollback < 2 mins, no customer-facing errors.

Pilot structure & standard asks (recommended asks to include in pilot acceptance email)
1) Scope: 30-day pilot for a single service route (conversation API) limited to non-production traffic.
2) Success criteria (pick 3):
   - 95th token latency < 200ms under 90th percentile traffic pattern,
   - Observed per-token unit cost reduction >= 25% after applying batching/quantization,
   - No critical security gaps as defined by the security checklist below.
3) Data and access: Provide test dataset (anonymized) and one infra contact with VPN/VPC peering privileges for Private/Dedicated pilots.
4) Ramp plan: Week 1 — integration and baseline profiling. Week 2 — enable KV/prefix caching and initial batching. Week 3 — apply quantization recommendations and run synthetic load. Week 4 — evaluate metrics and handoff to customer SRE.

Sample pilot pricing scenarios (playbook numbers for discussion; customize per customer)
- Sandbox Hosted pilot: Free-tier credits + metered usage. Typical engagement cost = $0–$2k (covering metered usage).
- Dedicated trial (30 days): Minimum commit equivalent to 0.5 GPU pool. Suggested billable: $12k flat (covers reserved capacity + ops support + 2 weekly runbooks).
- Private on-prem trial (30–60 days): Professional services + packaging fee. Suggested starting ask: $25k (includes packaging, airgap validation, and 1 week on-site enablement).

Pitch deck outline (one-slide descriptions to put in a customer-facing deck)
- Slide 1 — Executive summary & ask (pilot duration, primary success metric, decision owner)
- Slide 2 — Customer problem statement (latency/cost/ops pain)
- Slide 3 — How Redwood solves it (runtime + routing + cost controls)
- Slide 4 — Proof points (latency, cost delta, case study snippet)
- Slide 5 — Pilot plan (timeline, roles, success criteria)
- Slide 6 — Security & compliance mapping (high level controls + required next steps)
- Slide 7 — Commercial ask & next steps (pricing scenario and decision timeline)

Concise case study vignette (one-paragraph you can read aloud)
- "A payments SaaS migrated customer-facing chat routing to Redwood Dedicated to reduce latency variance and control unit costs. After a 45-day pilot they achieved a 35% reduction in per-interaction cost and reduced 99th-percentile latency by 120ms. Deployment used Dedicated capacity with regional fallbacks and an automated rollback policy; the customer moved to a 12-month reserved capacity the following quarter."

Security FAQ (short, mapped to common prospect checkpoints)
- Q: What deployment models protect customer data?
  A: Hosted (data in tenant buckets, encrypted at rest), Dedicated (isolated GPU pool with customer network controls), Private (customer-managed control plane or on-prem packaging). All models support KMS/HSM integrations for key control.
- Q: Can audit logs be exported to our SIEM?
  A: Yes — audit logging can be forwarded via syslog, S3 sinks, or API pull to your SIEM. Retention windows are configurable per contract.
- Q: How do you handle model provenance and model-change alerts?
  A: All model versions are cataloged with verifiable provenance. Platform supports automated quality checks on rollouts and can trigger regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
- Q: What certifications are available?
  A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II for the control plane. Private deployments inherit customer controls; we provide evidence packages for ISO/SOC/PCI conversations on request.
- Q: What is the incident response model for pilot customers?
  A: For pilots, we assign a named technical lead, provide a runbook for escalation and a 4-hour P1 response target during business hours. Dedicated/Enterprise SLAs are contractual.

Objection handling cheatsheet (two-line counters)
- "We built our own runtime": Counter — "We see 6–9 months of steady effort to reach parity on batching, KV cache correctness, and cost-aware routing. We provide the same controls with far lower operational risk and built-in rollbacks to protect users while you iterate."
- "Vendor lock-in concerns": Counter — "Redwood’s API and rollout artifacts are exportable; you can pin model versions and export cache keys and config to a shim layer if you decide to move."

Assets to attach to pilot proposal (checklist)
- One-page latency & cost benchmark PDF (tailored to the prospect model class)
- Short video walkthrough (8–12 minutes) of: integration, telemetry views, and rollback demo
- Security checklist with evidence links (SOC2 report excerpt, audit logging config example)
- Quickstart repo for platform engineers with sample IaC snippets (VPC peering, KMS example)

Ownership & next steps
- Internal owner: Platform GTM (Priya Menon) — owns playbook updates and pilot pricing exceptions.
- For each pilot: assign a Redwood technical lead and a commercial owner. Use kickoff template: kickoff-template.md in the Deal Docs repo.
- Follow-up cadence: Weekly tech sync + biweekly executive check-in for pilots longer than 60 days.

Appendix: example IaC snippet (text table for quick reference)
- VPC peering: Describe peering steps, subnet ranges, route config, and required security groups.
- KMS integration: Key ARN, grant policy pattern, rotation cadence recommendations.

Document maintenance: review this playbook quarterly or after any major pricing or SLA change.
